answer: Each candidate identity must complete a prescribed sequence of modular squarings, with each result required before the next can be computed. GPUs may run separate chains, but cannot divide one chain’s dependency sequence to remove its delay; simulating many clones therefore requires parallel hardware and time for each. This makes identity creation costly, while a Wesolowski proof enables compact verification. The vault stays protected across the horizon, even if an attacker mines shale for more compute.
